faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before you start
faq.a1: PyraSuite is an AI marketing studio for restaurants, shops and clinics in the UAE and the Gulf. Type your idea in Arabic and Pyra — the platform's engine — turns it into product photos, posts with captions, a marketing plan, a competitor analysis and a voiceover in your dialect. Nine studios, one subscription, a transparent credit system.
faq.q2: How does the credit system work?
faq.a2: Every action has a clear cost you see before you click. One image = 1 credit, a full 9-post campaign = 12. No surprises — and if a generation fails, the credits return to your account automatically.
faq.q3: How do I try the platform?
faq.a3: Sign up with your email for free and start immediately — no invites, no waiting. Your account gets {credits} credits to try the studios, and no credit card is needed.
faq.q4: Does Pyra AI really understand Arabic?
faq.a4: It doesn't just understand it — it's built Arabic-first. Write in Gulf, Egyptian, Levantine, or Modern Standard Arabic. Pyra AI gets the context and creates content that sounds natural, not translated.
faq.a5: Monthly subscription credits renew every month. Top-up credits stay valid for 12 months — buy them and use them at your own pace.
faq.q6: What happens if I run out of credits?
faq.a6: You can top up extra credits anytime without changing your plan. Or upgrade to a bigger plan — one click from the billing page.
faq.a7: Anytime. No contracts, no commitments, no questions asked. Cancel from the billing page and you're done.
faq.a8: Yes — the interface is available in both Arabic and English. But the real strength is that Pyra AI is designed Arabic-first, not translated from English.

creator.step1: Write what you have in mind, in Arabic — "a shawarma wrap that makes people hungry, for my restaurant in Dubai".
creator.step2: Pick the platform and the style. Pyra takes your business and city from your Brand Kit; you do not type them again.
creator.step3: Download it, or take it further in the Image Editing studio.
creator.q1: Does it render Arabic correctly on the image?
creator.a1: Yes. Letters come out joined, in their correct contextual forms, right to left, with no diacritics you did not ask for. This was the hardest thing in the product, and there is an explicit rule stopping Pyra inventing text anywhere else in the frame.
creator.q2: Do I need to write a professional prompt?
creator.a2: No. We ran both against the same request: a short colloquial Arabic sentence produced a better image than a carefully written English brief naming lens, aperture and lighting. Write the way you speak.
creator.q3: Is the image the right size for the platform?
creator.a3: Yes. You pick the platform and the canvas follows it — square, Instagram's 4:5 portrait, or wide. The picture is composed for that frame from the start rather than cropped into it afterwards.

photoshoot.name: Product Photography
photoshoot.tagline: One phone photo of your product — a full shoot back
photoshoot.definition: PyraSuite's Product Photography studio takes one photo of your product from your phone and returns 1, 3 or 6 frames, each with its own camera, composition and styling — front hero, three-quarter, overhead flat lay, macro detail, side profile and elevated — in whichever of seven ready-made environments you pick.
photoshoot.metaTitle: Product Photography — a full shoot from one phone photo
photoshoot.metaDescription: Upload one photo of your product and get six frames at different angles and lighting, with no studio, no photographer and no backdrop. See real output and the price before you sign up.
photoshoot.step1: Upload one photo of your product. An ordinary phone photo is enough — the product just has to be visible.
photoshoot.step2: Pick the environment: white studio, food, lifestyle, nature, urban, luxury or festive. Then pick how many frames.
photoshoot.step3: Download the frames, or take any one of them into the Image Editing studio if you need it to a marketplace specification.
photoshoot.q1: Do I need a professional photographer?
photoshoot.a1: No. You give Pyra one photo of your product and it builds the set, the lighting and the angle. Each of the six frames has its own written camera, composition and styling — front hero, three-quarter, overhead flat lay, macro on the detail, side profile and elevated — and the product being photographed is the one in your photo, not something that resembles it.
photoshoot.q2: Are the images good enough for Amazon and noon?
photoshoot.a2: For your catalogue and your social feed, yes — and the white studio environment gives you a seamless white backdrop with no horizon line and no props. But a marketplace main image has a written specification, and the two disagree: Amazon wants a square, noon wants a 2:3 portrait. That is the Image Editing studio's job; it carries a preset for each that sets the canvas and the background to spec.
photoshoot.q3: How many frames do I get?
photoshoot.a3: You choose 1, 3 or 6, and the price moves with them — it is stated above. If a frame never arrives, Pyra returns its share to your balance automatically and you are not charged for it.

edit.name: Image Editing
edit.tagline: Your product untouched — the background and the canvas to spec
edit.definition: PyraSuite's Image Editing studio takes the product photo you already have and changes one thing about it from a ready-made preset instead of a written prompt: a pure white background to the Amazon or noon specification, props removed, colour matched to your brand, or Arabic text set onto the product itself — while the product and the print already on it stay exactly as they are.
edit.metaTitle: Image Editing — marketplace white backgrounds, done to spec
edit.metaDescription: Put your product photo on an Amazon- or noon-ready white background, or set Arabic text onto the product itself — from a preset, not a prompt. See a real before and after.
edit.step1: Upload the photo you already have — the same product shot you took on your phone.
edit.step2: Pick the preset: marketplace white background, props removed, brand colour match, or Arabic text on the product.
edit.step3: Download the new image and put it on your store or your social feed.
edit.q1: Will it change how my product looks?
edit.a1: No. The governing rule in this studio is that your product's shape, colours, materials and the print on its packaging stay exactly as they are, and only what you asked for changes. See the before and after above: the same date-syrup jar, from a busy café to a white background, its label untouched — both frames from one real run.
edit.q2: Can it remove the background and make it white?
edit.a2: Yes, and it is the most valuable thing on the list. There is a preset for Amazon and one for noon because their specifications disagree: Amazon wants a square with the product filling the frame, noon wants a 2:3 portrait with the product at 70–80% of the frame height. After the image comes back we walk the background itself and set it to exactly 255 white — because near-white is not white to a marketplace.
edit.q3: Can I put Arabic text on the product?
edit.a3: Yes. You type the exact words, and Pyra sets them on the product or its packaging, correctly joined and right to left, without inventing any other text elsewhere in the frame. This was run against production: the text landed on the wrapper itself, following its folds in the same printed ink, with the existing print untouched.

plan.name: Marketing Plan
plan.tagline: A 30, 60 or 90-day plan for your business, with a budget and a content calendar
plan.definition: PyraSuite's Marketing Plan studio takes your business name, industry, audience and budget and returns a written plan for the period you choose: objectives that each carry a KPI and a target number, the budget split across channels by percentage, a week-by-week content calendar covering the whole period, and KPIs to measure it — and you can download it as a PDF.
plan.metaTitle: Marketing Plan — a 30/60/90-day marketing plan for your business
plan.metaDescription: Fill in your details and get a written marketing plan: objectives with numbers, the budget split by channel, and a weekly content calendar. See a real sample and the price before you sign up.
plan.step1: Enter your business name, industry, audience and monthly budget.
plan.step2: Pick the period — 30, 60 or 90 days — and set your goals.
plan.step3: Read the plan on screen, then download it as a PDF for your team or your partner.
plan.q1: Does the plan actually cover the period I picked?
plan.a1: Yes, and that is measured rather than assumed. The calendar is split week by week, one entry per week for as many weeks as your period runs — 30 days is four weeks numbered 1 to 4 — and that number is written out in the instruction Pyra receives rather than left to its judgement.
plan.q2: Is the plan generic, or about my business?
plan.a2: About your business. If your brand identity carries a description and a city, Pyra reads them and builds on them. In a real production run the identity said the restaurant was in Karama, and the plan that came back called for "geo-targeted ads within a 5km radius of Karama" — a word that appeared nowhere in the request.
plan.q3: Does the plan come out in Arabic?
plan.a3: It comes out in the language you are working in. Every plan used to be generated in Arabic whatever your language; that is fixed, and the page now sends the language with the request. The sample above was generated in English because that run was an English one.

analysis.name: Marketing Analysis
analysis.tagline: See yourself and see your competitors — before you spend on an ad
analysis.definition: PyraSuite's Marketing Analysis studio takes a description of your business, your audience and your competitors' names, and returns an analysis in five parts: a SWOT of strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats; your audience personas; a competitor table with each one's strengths and weaknesses; a 30, 60 and 90-day roadmap; and KPIs that each carry a target number and a timeframe.
analysis.metaTitle: Marketing Analysis — SWOT and competitor analysis for your business
analysis.metaDescription: A SWOT, audience personas, a competitor table and a 30/60/90-day roadmap, written for the Gulf market. See a real sample and the price before you sign up.
analysis.step1: Describe your business and your audience, and add up to three competitor names.
analysis.step2: Write down the problems you can see in your marketing today — those are what steer the analysis.
analysis.step3: Move through the five tabs, then download the analysis as a PDF.
analysis.q1: Do I need to know my competitors' names?
analysis.a1: It is better if you do, because the competitor table is built from the names you type — the strengths, weaknesses and share of each one. Without them the rest of the analysis still works, but that part comes back weaker.
analysis.q2: Does the analysis understand the market we are in?
analysis.a2: The instruction Pyra receives says in as many words to include Gulf and MENA market context, whatever language you are reading in. The sample above is a real analysis of a shawarma restaurant in Dubai, and its threats are written about operating costs in Dubai and about the delivery apps.
analysis.q3: Do the KPIs come back as numbers, or as vague statements?
analysis.a3: As numbers. Every KPI comes back with a metric, a target number and a timeframe — "direct orders as a share of the total, 20%, 90 days". This was broken for a while: the instruction asked for fields under different names from the ones the screen read, so the headline number rendered blank. It is fixed, and the sample above is the result.

storyboard.name: Storyboard
storyboard.tagline: One video idea — nine scenes you can hand to any videographer
storyboard.definition: PyraSuite's Storyboard studio takes your video idea, its length, the platform and the style, and returns nine scenes in order: each with a visual description, the line of dialogue or voice-over, the camera angle and its movement, its length in seconds, and the mood and suggested music — and the scene lengths add up to the duration you asked for.
storyboard.metaTitle: Storyboard — nine video scenes with camera angles and dialogue
storyboard.metaDescription: Turn a video idea into nine ready scenes: visual description, dialogue, camera angle and movement, and the length of each scene. See a real sample and the price before you sign up.
storyboard.step1: Write the video idea and pick its length — 15, 30 or 60 seconds.
storyboard.step2: Pick the style: cinematic, UGC, animation or documentary. Then the platform — Reels, TikTok, YouTube or TV.
storyboard.step3: Download the storyboard as a PDF for your videographer or editor, or take the dialogue into the Voiceover studio.
storyboard.a1: Nine, not fewer. The instruction asks for exactly nine, and the result is checked before you are charged — if fewer than nine come back the run counts as failed and your balance is returned in full. This was broken before: the check accepted a single scene.
storyboard.a2: The dialogue and voice-over come back in the language you are working in. The visual description stays in English on purpose, because it is written to be handed to an image model or to a videographer. The sample above has Arabic dialogue and English camera angles, and that is what the real output looks like.
storyboard.q3: Can I turn it straight into a video?
storyboard.a3: No. A storyboard is a working document — scenes, angles and dialogue — not a video. Video generation is not in the product today and we do not sell it. What you can do is shoot the scenes or hand them to an editor, and take the dialogue into the Voiceover studio.

prompt-builder.name: Prompt Assistant
prompt-builder.tagline: Cannot describe what you have in mind? Write it plainly and get three ready briefs
prompt-builder.definition: PyraSuite's Prompt Assistant takes one plain Arabic sentence about what you want and returns three English briefs that differ in approach rather than in wording — each with a style name and an Arabic tip telling you when to use it. This studio is free and takes nothing off your balance.
prompt-builder.metaTitle: Prompt Assistant — turn a plain sentence into a professional brief, free
prompt-builder.metaDescription: Write what you want in plain Arabic and get three ready image-generation briefs, each in a different style with an Arabic tip. Completely free. See a real sample.
prompt-builder.step1: Write what you want in plain language — "professional photos of a glass honey jar for an online shop".
prompt-builder.step2: Pick the kind of output you are heading for: image, video, copy or campaign.
prompt-builder.step3: Read the three, take the closest one, and use it in any studio.
prompt-builder.a1: Yes, with no conditions. This studio is priced at zero in the product's own cost table in code, so it never reaches the balance-deduction path at all. You can use it on the free plan without anything coming off your balance.
prompt-builder.q2: Why does the brief come back in English?
prompt-builder.a2: Because that is what image models understand best. You write in plain Arabic and the result comes back in English so you can paste it into any image tool — but the tip beside each brief comes back in Arabic, so you can choose without reading English.
prompt-builder.a3: They should be, and the instruction says in as many words that the three must differ in approach rather than being rephrasings — because three rephrasings of one idea give you one option, not three. Look at the sample above: one minimalist studio, one modern luxury, one natural daylight.
